title: A laid-out piece names the byte of the source it starts at
body:
`layout` and `layout_marked` return rows of `(String, Style)` pieces. A piece carries its look and, for link text, its link's index in `Style::link`, but nothing ties it to the text `parse` read. A program that lays out a document with `cmr` cannot tell which bytes of the markdown a cell on screen came from.

coax needs that to let a person mark a passage of an agent's reply and send the agent the passage's markdown: backticks, link targets and list markers included.

## Proposal

- `Style` gains `source: Option<usize>`: the byte offset, in the text given to `parse`, of the piece's first character, when the piece's text is a verbatim slice of that text. That covers text in headings, paragraphs, list items, table cells and quotes, plus inline code, bold text, link text and code block lines.
- `source` is `None` for anything `cmr` draws itself: bullets and list numbers, quote bars, code gutters and headers, table borders and padding, rules, and spaces added at a join or a wrap.
- A piece split by wrapping or cut by a column keeps the offset of its own first character.
- Offsets stay relative to the whole text inside nested quotes and list items.
close_reason: Landed in 48ac8bc. Style::source holds each piece's starting byte. Inline::Text, Inline::Code and Block::Code carry the offsets from parse to layout.
